title: The build store keeps every npm package it is given, which slows every install through it
foundBy: session agent, investigating campaign's failed `make repin` of 2026-09-29

evidence.verified: dashboards' tests/test_record_build.py passes 18 of 18 against this record-build.sh, byte for byte, and its prune test fails against the previous copy. Run over a copy of the owner's store, the prune took npm/ from 179 packages (311 MB) to 47 (83 MB), keeping each project's three newest.

resolution: Each recorded build removes the npm packages of older ones. A project keeps them for its three newest builds recorded within three days, and for its newest whatever its age. Entries, modules and images stay, and a store that is a repository, as a campaign's is, is left whole.
details: Nothing removed npm packages from the owner's build store. Each clean `make ci` in lint, ledger or npmrevs adds five there, and `npm run ci` in ui adds one. The cs-npmrevs registry reads every package it serves before it answers, and `scripts/with-npmrevs.sh` serves the store, so each build made every later install through it wait longer. By 2026-09-29 the store held 179 packages (311 MB), the registry took about 9 seconds to start, and campaign's `make repin` failed waiting for it. This project records no npm package, but it carries the same script, so a build recorded here is a moment the store can be pruned.
